clue.text: Darn! Accepting credit leading to ruin

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the next piece into its middle

parts.note: to darn is to sew up a hole
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
leading means ahead, as a team two goals up

explanation.surface: Someone swears as running up credit drags them towards financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn!' reads as a mild oath, but it is the mending verb; 'to' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up something is an informal idiom for spoiling or wrecking it completely.

clue.text: Case of stout ready in bar

indicators.note: case of means only the outside letters of stout, its casing, are used

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit to eat

explanation.surface: A crate of stout beer is ready to serve in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub to go with the stout; it is a band of colour. 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour, which is also called a bar.

clue.text: Negligent about failure

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a failure to hit

explanation.surface: Someone careless about a mistake they have made.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss describes someone lax and careless in their duty.

clue.text: Feller with glasses at Washington, right?

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
DC, District of Columbia, is Washington
right in the British sense 'a right mess', meaning utter or complete

explanation.surface: A bespectacled bloke in Washington is asking for confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for fellow; it is one who fells trees. 'at' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcutter fells trees for timber, so is literally a person who fells.

clue.text: Go quietly, American pig!

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as does pep
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal telling an American to leave without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig' reads as an insult; Peppa Pig is a British children's cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppa is the cartoon pig who stars in the children's television series named after her.

clue.text: Arguments about a 9's impositions

indicators.note: about means the word for arguments goes around the other pieces

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels
the answer to 9 across is the NATO alphabet's code word for the letter R

explanation.surface: Quarrels over the taxes a ninth party has imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 across answer, ROMEO, is the radio code word for R. TIFFS goes around A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties or charges imposed on goods, so impositions in the sense of levies.

clue.text: Cheers — doctor keeps half of hair gel

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
half of means only the first two letters of hair are kept

explanation.surface: Thanks given to a medic who stocks some hair-styling product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' looks like hair product to go with the surface; it is the verb meaning to come together. KEEPS with HA is shuffled to KESHAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: When plans gel they set or take definite form, the idiom meaning to develop into shape.

clue.text: Rebel forces Irish division raised

indicators.note: raised means the letters are read upwards in this down entry
division indicates the answer lies across the split between the two words

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel army division is mobilised.
explanation.walkthrough: ESIR sits across 'forces Irish'; read upwards, it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up is to revolt, so rebel as a verb means to rise against authority.

clue.text: See 8
Fight a persistent battle, getting furious

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptically: a long pillow fight leaves you literally ... out ...
second meaning: very angry, the British idiom

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful picture of a drawn-out pillow fight; 'getting' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting feathers is a British idiom for being extremely angry, or very thirsty.

clue.text: Capital! Old guy playing the field

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An exclamation of approval for an elderly man still dating around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation meaning excellent; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A romeo is a womaniser, after Shakespeare's lover, one who dates many partners.

clue.text: Countryman rejected home at deer park, originally

indicators.note: rejected means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: in means at home
the sika is a species of deer

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of park is used

explanation.surface: A man from the country turned down a home in a deer park.
explanation.walkthrough: Build INATSIKAP from IN, AT, SIKA and P, then read it backwards; 'Countryman' means a compatriot of a particular country, not a rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a national of Pakistan, a man of that country in the citizen sense.

clue.text: So cheap it's ridiculous, this previous form of transport

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are absurdly jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned way of travelling is described as absurdly inexpensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A post chaise was a hired horse-drawn carriage used for fast travel before railways.

clue.text: Note cocaine and smack

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
a smack is a hit

explanation.surface: A message about two hard drugs, smack being heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' suggests heroin beside cocaine; here it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short written memo or voucher, such as a signed slip for a debt.

clue.text: Ready to include north? People involved in it having second thoughts

indicators.note: to include means the letter for north goes inside the word for ready

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: involved in means the people are placed within the word it

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to bring in the north, as those involved reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second thoughts' looks like a single phrase, but 'second' gives S and 'thoughts' alone is the definition. 'having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiments are views or opinions, the feelings a person holds about something.

clue.text: Figure's toned and rather developed

definitions.note: read as 'figure is', the definition is the figure

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone's body has become toned and rather well developed at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person's physique; it is a geometric solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a solid shape with four triangular faces, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Persecute Francesca on the stage wearing rubber

indicators.note: wearing means the actress's surname is enclosed by the word for rubber, as if dressed in it

parts.note: a tyre is made of rubber
Francesca Annis is an English stage and screen actress

explanation.surface: An actress performing in a rubber costume is being harassed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tyrannise is to rule or treat others cruelly and oppressively, to persecute them.

clue.text: Savage taking too many drugs in comic novel

indicators.note: in means the whole savage piece goes inside the word for comic

parts.note: a wit is a comedian

indicators.note: taking means the savage swallows the overdose

parts.note: Hun, from the invaders, means a savage person
OD is an overdose

explanation.surface: A wild man overdosing in a funny book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic novel' wants to be one phrase, but 'comic' is a joker and the novel is a crime story.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective novel, a book whose plot asks who committed the crime.

clue.text: Kabul was gutted, right? Rebuilt defensive fortifications

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new order
gutted means the insides of was are removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Afghanistan's capital was destroyed, so its walls were reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' applies only to 'was', leaving WS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulwarks are ramparts or defensive walls protecting a town.

clue.text: Are sure to be in trouble during army detention

indicators.note: during means the jumbled letters sit within the word for army

parts.note: a host is a large army

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of are sure are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Soldiers are certain to get into bother while confined to barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' is a host in the old sense of a great multitude of soldiers; 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: House arrest is confinement to one's home by authorities, a form of detention.

clue.text: Ambassador's sister vicious at heart

definitions.note: read as 'ambassador is', the definition is the ambassador

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of vicious are taken

explanation.surface: A diplomat's sibling is cruel deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy, the Vatican's equivalent of an ambassador.

clue.text: Nurse invites the man inside (that's all there is)

indicators.note: invites, with inside, means the man is brought into the word for nurse
inside means the pronoun is placed within the other piece

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A nurse asks a man in, with a bracketed remark that nothing more follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed phrase is the definition, shown as the final words of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The end is the closing phrase of a film or book, said when nothing more remains.

clue.text: Miserable reason for 8 7?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: having soft feathers (...) in your mouth would make you spit out feathers

explanation.walkthrough: 8 7 is SPITTING FEATHERS; read literally, a mouthful of down is why you would spit feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down in the mouth is an idiom for looking gloomy and dejected.

clue.text: See 21
Might one be spotted laughing?

parts.note: the spotted and the laughing are both names for one African scavenger

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether someone could be caught laughing; 'spotted' and 'laughing' are both adjectives naming the same animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is also called the laughing hyena, after its cackling call.

clue.text: One about to make an alliance

indicators.note: about means the article is turned back to front

parts.note: an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single person is on the brink of forming a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as a phrase meaning ready to; 'about' reverses AN and 'to' stays itself. 'make an' links.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance of Western nations.

clue.text: Make standard inside Scandinavian country

indicators.note: inside means the country's name sits within the word for Scandinavian

parts.note: Norse means of Scandinavia
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A regulation from within some Nordic country to impose uniformity.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring something into line with a norm or regular state.

clue.text: Good hotel described as having limited appeal

indicators.note: described in the sense of drawn around, so the word for good encircles the letter

parts.note: nice means good or pleasant
H is the NATO alphabet's letter for hotel

explanation.surface: A decent hotel is said to attract only a select clientele.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' is used in its geometric sense, to draw a line around. 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche product or market appeals to a small specialised section of people.

clue.text: Silk in south-east courts not about to work

indicators.note: to work means the letters are worked over into a fresh arrangement
not means the letter for about is left out of the word courts

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A barrister in the south-east is not in court, not about to work.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a silk is a senior barrister, which the courts help suggest. COURTS without C is OURTS, which with SE is rearranged; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse brownish silk from wild silkworms, a fabric rather than a lawyer.

clue.text: Split from a rubbish Tory department

parts.note: BS is short for bullshit, meaning rubbish
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A Conservative ministry splits from a worthless party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a division in the party; it is slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is slang for leaving suddenly, and to abscond is to run off secretly.
